clue.text: What represents zero score? Love

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batter out without scoring has made a nought, called by this bird's name
a British term of endearment, as in 'all right, love?'

explanation.surface: A tennis question: what stands for nil in the scoring? Love.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers you to tennis, where love is zero; but the zero score here is the cricketer's, and 'Love' is the second definition, a British pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket calls a batter's nought by this bird's name, and in northern England the same word is an affectionate form of address like dear.

clue.text: One of 16 joining party to punt

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
to punt is to bet, so a punt is a wager

explanation.surface: A woman joins a party set for a flutter on the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: '16' refers to the solution of 16-down, former students who were girls; colloquially the phrase also means an elderly woman, which is what this word suggests. 'punt' is the British slang for a bet, not the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled widow of advanced years is the stock picture of a grand elderly lady, which the colloquial phrase at 16 also describes.

clue.text: United in friendship, kin squashed into small room

indicators.note: the word into tells us the jumbled kin is placed inside the small room

parts.note: a closet is a small room or cupboard

indicators.note: squashed suggests the letters of kin are crushed out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Relatives crammed into a tiny room become a tight little group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashed' does two things in the surface, cramming and crushing; here it jumbles 'kin', and 'into' is the separate signal for putting that jumble inside the small room.
explanation.definitionFit: A tightly bound group whose members are mutually supportive is described with this knitting image of stitches drawn close together.

clue.text: Letter-opener produced by Eppie and Frank working together

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and recombined as one pool

explanation.surface: Two people named Eppie and Frank collaborate to make a desk tool for slitting envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working together' signals an anagram of EPPIE and FRANK combined; 'and' and 'produced by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt blade used to slit envelopes is the desk tool also called a letter-opener; the two names are synonyms.

clue.text: Smart chap given to fury

parts.note: a smart alec is a know-all, so the smart chap is named Alec
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clever fellow is prone to losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fury' looks like a common noun for rage, but it means one of the three Furies of Greek myth, avenging goddesses; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology she is one of the three Erinyes, avenging goddesses known in English as the Furies.

clue.text: Encourage nippers to come out of their shells using these

definitions.text: Encourage nippers to come out of their shells using these

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage or urge
teeth nip, so they are nippers

explanation.surface: Coax shy children out of their shells by means of these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nippers' reads as British slang for young children, but it means biters; the whole clue also defines the hard tip a chick uses to break out of its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatchling birds and reptiles grow a small hard point on the beak or snout to crack the shell, then shed it.

clue.text: Talks, I heard, are failing in region of Southern Africa

indicators.note: failing suggests the words have broken down and collapsed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reports that negotiations are breaking down somewhere in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges the fourteen letters of TALKS I HEARD ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: This arid sandy expanse covers much of Botswana and parts of Namibia and South Africa.

clue.text: I am given time to produce sculpture

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A sculptor claims that with enough time they will produce a statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' and 'to produce' are links joining the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or modelled likeness of a person is a representation, so a statue is a kind of likeness.

clue.text: Record headless monkey in city of Asia Minor

parts.note: EP stands for extended play, a type of record

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the monkey's name is cut off

parts.note: the rhesus is a macaque monkey

explanation.surface: Someone records a decapitated monkey in an ancient Anatolian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' drops R from RHESUS, leaving HESUS.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Greek city on the Aegean coast of Anatolia was famed for its Temple of Artemis and St Paul's epistle.

clue.text: Making poetic address, and adding punctuation?

definitions.meaning: in rhetoric, to turn aside and speak directly to an absent person or thing, as poets do
jocularly, inserting the mark used for possession and contraction

explanation.surface: A poet declaims to the moon, and also sprinkles commas about.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense as a playful literal reading of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhetorical figure of addressing someone absent shares its name with the raised comma, so the verb fits both declaiming and punctuating.

clue.text: Expression of delight with little toy brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the toy is placed inside the word for little

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small
a hoop is a toy rolled along or swung round the waist

explanation.surface: A child cries out happily on being given a small toy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' is Scots and British informal for small; 'with' is just a link, though it tempts you to take W from it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an exclamation of exuberant joy, a cry like hurrah.

clue.text: Giant pig's round shadow stretched to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, extending westwards means reading right to left
round means the pig's word goes around the shadow's word

parts.note: a hog is a pig; the 's is a link
to shadow someone is to follow them, which is to tail them

explanation.surface: A huge pig's rounded shadow lengthens westward at sunset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretched to the west' reverses the whole pig-round-shadow assembly, since an across entry reads east. 'shadow' is the verb sense, to follow someone, not a dark shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philistine champion slain by David with a sling is the byword for a huge person.

clue.text: Touring Wales, here he gets help to make things run smoothly

definitions.text: help to make things run smoothly

indicators.note: touring suggests the letters travel about and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A man touring Wales finds people who help him get around smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' signals an anagram of WALES HERE HE GETS, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from oiling axles: to ease a process along, often with money or favours.

clue.text: Following river away from source, divers get exhausted

indicators.note: following means the next piece comes after the river's letter
away from source means the first letter of the word is removed, as a river runs from its spring

parts.note: divers is an old word for various, as is sundry

explanation.surface: Downstream from a river's source, divers find the water running out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not people diving but the archaic adjective for sundry; 'away from source' drops its S to leave UNDRY, which follows R.
explanation.definitionFit: A well or supply that runs out of water is used up, so the phrase means become spent.

clue.text: People transfixed about king in the buff

indicators.note: about means the transfixed people surround the king's letter

parts.note: people transfixed by something stare, so they are starers
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Onlookers stand frozen around a king who is naked, as in the fable of the emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' means naked; the answer is jocular British slang for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: This jokey British slang means stark naked, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Cut out to cheer, I am popular in that

indicators.note: in tells us the two pieces go inside the word for cheer, referred to as that

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or delight
I am contracts to I'm
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: To cut someone out of a group and cheer about it: 'I'm popular in that.'
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to the word for cheer, the container named just before; 'I am' contracts as in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or exclude something completely, such as a team from a contest, is to excise it.

clue.text: Former students rig dolls out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and reassembled

explanation.surface: Ex-pupils dress up their dolls in an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals an anagram of RIG and DOLLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who attended a particular school are its alumnae, known in Britain by this phrase.

clue.text: To penetrate sect, a listening device is one weapon

indicators.note: to penetrate means the following pieces go inside the word for sect

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect
a tap is a bug fitted to a phone line

explanation.surface: Agents infiltrate a religious group, a bugging device being one of their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is one' links the wordplay to the definition; 'sect' suggests infiltrating a group, which is the container picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with elastic, or a siege engine, both hurl missiles, so either is an instrument of attack.

clue.text: In the circumstances, express disapproval of US train crew's accommodation

indicators.note: In means the disapproving sound is placed inside the word for circumstances

parts.note: a case is a set of circumstances, as in 'in that case'
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Under the conditions, someone grumbles about where an American train's crew must sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the circumstances' looks like a set phrase, but 'In' is the container signal and 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On North American freight trains the last wagon housed the crew, a van called this.

clue.text: Off course? Bill's fault

parts.note: an ad is an advertising bill or poster; the 's is a link
a rift is a fault or fracture in rock

explanation.surface: Someone has gone astray, and Bill is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a person, but it is a poster; 'fault' is a geological crack, not blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting with no mooring has wandered from its route, and figuratively the word means aimless.

clue.text: Scene of military activity in that place, occupied by mounted soldiers

indicators.note: occupied by means the place-word holds the soldiers inside it

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: mounted means going up, which in a down clue reads the soldiers' letters upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British part-time soldiers

explanation.surface: A battlefield there is held by cavalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' suggests cavalry, but in a down entry it means reading the Territorial Army's letters upwards before they go inside the place-word.
explanation.definitionFit: A region where fighting takes place is a battle zone, as in a theatre of war.

clue.text: Expedition visits a far island's interior

indicators.note: interior means the answer lies in the inside of the run of words

explanation.surface: A tour party calls in at the inland parts of a remote island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'viSITS A FAR Island's'; 'visits' and 'interior' look like travel terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey to observe or hunt wild animals, especially in East Africa, is a trek of this kind.

clue.text: Deer and rabbits seen in this part of country briefly

definitions.text: Deer and rabbits seen in this part of country briefly

parts.words: Deer and rabbits seen in this part of country briefly
parts.note: male deer and male rabbits are both called bucks, and that plural is the short name of an English county

explanation.surface: A wildlife spotter notes deer and rabbits glimpsed in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a nature report; the trick is that the plural word for male deer and rabbits is the county's standard abbreviation, Bucks. It lies north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This home county north-west of London is shortened to Bucks, the plural for male deer and rabbits.

clue.text: I left hot food finally to get cold

indicators.note: left means the letter has gone away from the word for the hot food
finally places the departing letter at the very end of that word

parts.note: chilli is a hot spicy dish or pepper

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the spicy dish until last, and it goes cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' and 'finally' remove the last I from CHILLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill is a coldness in the air, so the word means coolness as a noun or cool as an adjective.

clue.text: Actor, one appearing in musical

indicators.note: appearing in means the numeral goes inside the musical's title

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Oliver Twist
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An actor lands a part in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated twentieth-century British actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, Lord Olivier was the leading English stage and film performer of his era.

clue.text: Jack and the others are hidden side by side

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is AB, an able seaman

indicators.note: hidden means the unit is tucked away inside the word for the others

parts.note: the rest are the others
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: A man is concealed alongside the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not the verb but the metric unit of area, a hundred square metres, symbol A; it goes inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking abreast means in line next to one another, level and level, so the phrase fits.

clue.text: Praising European Union in respect of troop movements

parts.note: logistics is the military organisation of moving and supplying troops

explanation.surface: Brussels is lauded for the way it handles moving its troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'Praising'; the rest is a straight charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of high praise, so the adjective means laudatory.

clue.text: Entertain a lot, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us the word for a lot is heard, not spelt

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's destiny

explanation.surface: Someone entertains a great deal, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'much' but means one's lot, destiny; the answer is often said to rhyme with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or lavishly host them with celebrations.
